posts.author: Misk-ivus
posts.body:
Hello! This is something I've been working on and updating for a while now, I'd love some feedback because I've been sorely lacking any, I've felt really good working on this! Me and my brother made everything except the music, which is placeholder and copyrighted.
-Non linear, decision based progression
-8-bit NES style visuals (Including lots of lovely black backgrounds)
-Challenging and fully animated enemies with memorable designs and attacks
-Limited healing, HP is a resource
-Comically patronizing Easy Mode
-And much, much more!
In Mayfly, you play as Tela, a young adult human who doesn't have much to do, yet. While saving the world or collecting the 8 shiny egg McGuffins is fully out of their reach, that doesn't mean they can't do anything. Their world is full of people to make, places to see, enemies to fight, and most importantly... Decisions to make!
While you could just wake up, go do the one thing you have to do, then go to bed. The game will just end like that, mostly because the summer and fall seasons haven't been implemented. But even when they are implemented, you can repeat that process two more times and then the game will end. Instead, you can explore the world however you'd like (after your one task is complete)! There's always something to do, people to follow. This is a world Tela is very familiar with, so you're gonna be playing catch-up.
The most challenging part of that are the enemies, weather that be animals, people who don't respect you (few people do but there's this little thing called "basic decency"), one thing is for certain, you're not above your enemies. Your stats aren't significantly better then the enemies you fight, and beyond that, almost all have devastating unique attacks that can tear you to shreds. And all damage is permanent, Hp is a resource. You cannot heal in battle, and you can only heal at any given save point once for 1/5th of your max Hp! You'll either have to get better gear or items, or stop fighting people. There's no inherit value in defeating enemies, they give no exp, but may give items, progression towards an objective, or just get them to stop bugging you. Try to avoid fighting animals generally, they just run away and give no rewards.
It's not all bad for you, as you have plenty of tools and items at your disposal! If you can find them... Weapons don't increase you stats, but instead grant new moves! You can even swap weapons in battle if you need a certain attack (or just threw away your hatchet to perform a powerful tomahawk attack). And while Hp healing items can't be used in battle, offensive items can provide tons of utility that weapons simply can't. And, if you go looking for them, allies may even join you, temporarily.
There are plenty of optional challenges to engage with, but also people to talk to, more will be revealed about the world and characters if you partake in these challenges and talk to these people. Though challenging, everything is possible, if something is too hard, you could try going somewhere else and getting some equipment and coming back with knowledge and power! If all these decisions and enemies and learning is too difficult, there's always Easy Mode, selectable when starting a new game... But fair warning, Easy Mode might change the game more than you expect...
With all that being said, I hope you enjoy! This has been a passion project for me, I've drawn every enemy, tile, face, character, made sure every route in the story doesn't break. There's more than 4 hours of content and multiple routes already playable.
Credits are available at areas where the demo doesn't continue, I will make sure to add them to the main menu next update, for now, here's the credits, and the game can be downloaded for windows (it may work on mac but the sound might not).
